notes.summary: queue.sendNowBehavior defaults to 'abort': "Send now" stops the running answer and sends the queued message at once, instead of moving it to the head of the queue.
notes.howTo: Nothing to do if "Send now" should send now. To keep the old behaviour (send it once the running answer ends), set queue: { sendNowBehavior: 'next' } on AiChatProvider. Tests that call sendNow during a run with the default config now see stop() called. Editing a queued message also focuses the text field (Enter saves, Escape cancels) and returns the focus to Edit afterwards.

notes.summary: The recording waveform shows the recent loudness as scrolling bars across the full width, drawn on a canvas in currentColor, instead of six bars moving with one level.
notes.howTo: Nothing to do. To color it, set color on [data-part="wave-container"] or an ancestor; to size it, give [data-element="waveform"] a height (default 24px). CSS that targeted the old span bars inside [data-element="waveform"] no longer applies and can be removed.

notes.summary: A page can declare what the user has open (useViewContext, registerViewContext); the chat sends it with each new user message as glirastesViewContext. Unchanged apps: nothing changes; while nothing is registered no field is sent.
notes.howTo: Optional. In a React page call useViewContext({ entity: { type: 'order', id: order.id }, label: order.number }) (null withdraws, unmounting too); outside React call registerViewContext('order-page', entry) from glirastes/browser and the returned function on leaving the page (name the view, no record id or personal data: the name shows in development warnings). One entry can hold an entity and a selection (at most 50 ids); unsaved is its own field. The type must be an entity type the request's tools declare (outputEntities / inputEntities; a selection of another type is dropped, the entry stays with its entity), ids exactly as the app has them, facts are kept only with a schema in the handler's viewContext.facts, route only as an explicit path and a hint; state from the URL query belongs in facts. Nothing is read from the URL. Sent by the bundled Vercel transport with every new user message (also the "continue" message after a cut-off answer, a clarification answer and a direct / command), read when it is sent (a queued message carries the view of its send time; an update and a send in one event handler send the previous entry). Continuations after the stream ended (approval resume, continueTurn, budget continuation) carry none; an automatic continuation started from the running request can repeat the first send's field, which the server ignores. When sent, the field replaces a glirastesViewContext of bodyExtras. Past 8 entries the first 8 win, and children register before parents. To turn it off: register nothing (or pass null), or set viewContext: false on the server (createAiChatHandler); there is no switch per chat instance. An own transport adds currentViewContext() as glirastesViewContext: { version: 1, current } itself. The runtime container keeps the server side off. Known limit with piiShield: keep personal data out of labels over 60 characters (changelog 0.25.0).

notes.summary: With viewContext on (the default), createAiChatHandler sends <view-context and </view-context in the text of user messages and their file names to the model as <view-context (ASCII spelling and its listed variants). Text and file names without the name view-context are byte-identical.
notes.howTo: Nothing to do. Only the model input changes, and only for user text or a file name that contains the name view-context: there for every tag the pattern matches (any case, whitespace, zero-width characters or a soft hyphen between < and the name or around the /, <view-context-…>; a typed < before the name becomes &lt;; in such text also a < before 64 or more whitespace or zero-width characters). The file name of a file part is escaped the same way, in the part and in its placeholder text. The PII shield and the intent classification of the pipeline mode get the original text (no file names); the guardrails, a custom streamHandler, the chat and the stream get the original text and file names. Not caught: full-width or look-alike characters (＜, homoglyphs, other hyphens), a line break or invisible character inside the name, control and bidi characters between < and the name (such as U+0001, U+007F, U+0085, U+200E, U+202E, U+2066; issue #218), entities such as <, a tag split across text parts or messages, the content of file attachments, tool call arguments of an approval continuation, the imitated header without tags, chat memory notes and summaries, tool results and assistant text. Messages the SDK writes itself (seen-objects memo, chat memory, view context block, budget continuation, final summary instruction) are never escaped. The block grants no permission either way: the server checks types, ids and facts on its own. With viewContext: false (and in the runtime container) nothing changes. Tests that assert the exact model input for user text containing <view-context need the escaped form.
